summary.title: Some career advice.
summary.one_liner: A list of Will Larson's career advice for software engineers, covering decisions, risk, compensation, relationships, and luck, with the caveat that some points contradict each other.
keywords: save money when times are good
takeaways: Career decisions are rarely permanent; returning from management to engineering is possible though not neutral.
Consider a portfolio of options rather than comparing one opportunity against your current situation.
Save aggressively when earnings jump, since high compensation may be hard to regain later; specialization can lower outside pay.
Try internal moves before external ones, and avoid moving more often than every couple of years unless in a bad situation.
Build prestige and discoverability over time, and collect lasting professional relationships, since people last longer than jobs.
summary.summary: Will Larson shares a numbered list of career advice aimed at software engineers, presented as personal synthesis rather than fixed rules. Topics include decision-making (measure before you leap, try internal moves first), financial risks (specialization and lifestyle inflation), growth (going broad early, not staying comfortable too long), and reputation (building prestige, being discoverable, keeping relationships). He notes that some points conflict and that luck plays a large role in careers. The page is a short personal essay with no code or technical content.
